intention: A user can correct a Supercharger session's start/end battery % inline on /supercharger-stats, and the correction immediately reaches vehicle_metrics because analytics reads the same table the edit writes.
request: MAG-19 — ALLOW EDITING Supercharger sessions. Chart YYYY-MM labels + Y-axis; remove Country column; show the four battery-% columns; add an inline Edit action writing start_battery_pct/end_battery_pct + battery_pct_source='user_verified' via PATCH; re-run the vehicle_metrics calculated fields as the manual-charge path does; no delete action; update the KB.

decisions.decision: analytics switches its Supercharger source from telemetry.supercharger_sessions to charging.charge_sessions
decisions.why: The edit must land where analytics reads or item 4d is a no-op. Switching beats adding a 4th source: one table owns a session's percentages, so no conflict rule is needed.

decisions.decision: start_battery_pct_est / end_battery_pct_est stay NULL; displayed as "—"
decisions.why: No SOC estimator exists (RM27 D11 descoped it), so freezing a snapshot would fabricate a drift log. Building an estimator is out of scope.

decisions.decision: inline htmx row swap for the edit UX
decisions.why: Matches the ticket's "inline on the record", reuses the page's existing fragment-swap pattern, and avoids a PATCH on accidental blur.

decisions.decision: ticket item 2 (remove the Country column) gets no tier
decisions.why: Already done: charging.Session has no CountryCode (RM29 D1) and RM30 tier 2 removed the column. Recorded so its absence is not read as a missed requirement.

decisions.decision: gateway work split into two tiers — display (3) and edit (4)
decisions.why: The display half depends on nothing and ships alone; only the edit needs tiers 1 and 2. One gateway tier would have blocked the visible win behind the whole roadmap.

decisions.decision: both analytics Supercharger reads move to charge_sessions -- vehicle_metrics AND the Wh/km RecentEfficiency read
decisions.why: telemetry.supercharger_sessions is the nightly mirror's source and nothing else's. Moving only the percentage path leaves one entity read from two tables.

decisions.decision: the missing charging SessionReader methods get their own tier 2; analytics becomes tier 3 and depends on it
decisions.why: charging.SessionReader has only the Between shape; analytics needs UpdatedSince and limit too. Both are charging code, so one tier cannot hold both modules.

decisions.decision: watermark migration DELETEs the supercharger_sessions cursor rows instead of renaming them to charge_sessions
decisions.why: Absent watermark = epoch (RM29 D7), so the nightly Reconcile backfills. Carrying the value risks skipping any charge_sessions row older than the inherited cursor.

decisions.decision: Decision 10 STANDS -- the watermark migration DELETEs the supercharger_sessions cursor rows; it does not UPDATE them in place
decisions.why: Carrying the cursor is load-bearing on the nightly mirror running; a stalled mirror strands rows behind it undetectably. DELETE costs ~nothing since the next pass re-reads everything anyway.

decisions.decision: corrected the roadmap's tier-3 table cell, which said UPDATE and contradicted Decision 10
decisions.why: The stale cell is what the leader dispatched from, producing a design that reversed a settled owner decision. Left uncorrected it would mislead the next session the same way.

decisions.decision: list-and-match resolves a session by ID; no new charging by-ID port
decisions.why: charging.SessionReader has only ListSessionsByVehicleBetween. A by-ID port would be charging code and spawn a tier 6. Mirrors fetchEntryVM's documented no-GetEntry shape.

decisions.decision: save verb is PATCH with strict body semantics: both keys required, empty=NULL, absent key=400
decisions.why: Owner chose PATCH over the gateway's PUT gold standard: the write is partial at the resource level (3 of ~18 columns). The 400 closes PATCH's partial-body invitation, which VerifySession would answer with a silent NULL.

decisions.decision: recalculation window is +/-1 day around the session's stop day, via a NEW helper
decisions.why: A session stopping between midnight and the ~03:30 poller hour belongs to the previous metric day (effectiveDay = CapturedDate-1). Matches Reconcile's own D8 widening. recalculateAfterChargeWrite is left alone.

decisions.decision: the day comes from ChargeStopDateTime, computed in UTC
decisions.why: sumSuperchargerPctBetween filters on ChargeStopDateTime; the page already rules plain UTC (D9a) and the gateway cannot see the poller's Location. The +/-1 window absorbs the zone error; the shifts cannot compound.

decisions.decision: TeslaID == nil: skip recalculation and log; the write still succeeds
decisions.why: VerifySession has no vehicle predicate, so a hand-built PATCH can return a nil TeslaID. Account-scoping is the security boundary and holds. Matches recalculateAfterChargeWrite's swallow-and-log posture.

decisions.decision: blank inputs clear a value; no end<start ordering validation
decisions.why: An irreversible verification UI is a trap, and VerifySession(nil,nil) clears the source too. Ordering is declined per tier 1 D8, which matches the table's deliberate absence of that CHECK. Only 0-100 is validated.

decisions.decision: new csrfSuperchargerKey; the page issues the token, fragments read it
decisions.why: csrfManualChargeKey is issued only by GET /charges and checkCSRFKey fails closed, so reuse would block any user arriving directly. A row-edit fragment issuing fresh would invalidate a second open row's token.

decisions.decision: KB update also corrects the now-false 'ONE concept with a user write path' cross-reference; file is not renamed
decisions.why: Leaving it would tell the next agent this page has no write path, one file from the write path we added. Renaming -read.md churns the INDEX and every inbound reference for a cosmetic gain.
